name: Advertising Council

summary.text: The Advertising Council, formed in wartime as the War Advertising Council, resumed its peacetime name after President Truman asked it to continue as a public-service organization. From 1949 it ran the 'Religion in American Life' campaign, under the sponsorship of Religion in American Life Inc., a New York group of business and professional people; the campaign continued until the Ad Council distanced itself in 1992.

sources.title: Doctoral dissertation on the Religion in American Life campaign (Henning, 1996)

facts.claim: The Ad Council's history says that after President Truman asked it to continue as a peacetime public-service organization, the War Advertising Council changed its name back to the Ad Council.
facts.quote: the War Advertising Council changed its name back to the Ad Council

facts.claim: A 1986 Christian Science Monitor report says the Religion in American Life ads ran under the low-profile sponsorship of Religion in American Life Inc., a nonprofit group of business and professional people based in New York active since 1949.
facts.quote: under the low-profile sponsorship of Religion in American Life Inc.

facts.claim: A 1996 University of Tennessee dissertation on the campaign says funding was a long-standing problem and contributed to the Ad Council distancing itself from RIAL in 1992.
facts.quote: funding for the campaign was a long-standing problem

sources.title: Doctoral dissertation on the Religion in American Life campaign (Henning, 1996)

connections.claim: The Ad Council produced the Religion in American Life campaign from 1949 under RIAL Inc.'s sponsorship.
connections.quote: under the low-profile sponsorship of Religion in American Life Inc.

sources.title: Doctoral dissertation on the Religion in American Life campaign (Henning, 1996)

openQuestions: The Ad Council's own history page did not surface the RIAL campaign; the Duke University Ad Council records list it. Named corporate backers of RIAL were not found in opened sources.
